title: Stability Loom: Ops Notes and Hour-by-Hour Sentinel (2026-04 Diary)
content:
Purpose and framing:
This is a working field diary for the upcoming micro-launch (canary cohort → regional ramp). The voice here is ops-first: compact, checklistable, and readable in a 30s glance. Use this during the 24h watch window.

High-level objectives:
- Maintain p95 inference latency <= 120ms for the canary flows.
- Keep error rate for generation endpoints < 0.5% above baseline (baseline = avg last 7 days).
- Validate KV/cache warmup reduces cold-token penalties after the first 10k requests.
- Collect targeted evals from the canary sample set for quality regressions.

Preflight (T-24h to T-1h) — short, actionable checks:
- Config and artifact sanity:
  - Model version pinned: model/redwood-7b-v2@2026-04-10 ✅
  - Config diff checked: autoscaler, batch_size override, timeout_ms=60000 ✅
  - Canary routing rule created (10% of internal traffic to canary pool) — RULE-ID: CAN-2026-04-12-a ✅
- Infra health:
  - GPU pool utilization baseline computed and documented in CONFLUENCE-3142 ✅
  - Node replacement window booked (if nodes need drain) — contact oncall-sre if >2 nodes drain simultaneously ✅
- Telemetry hooks:
  - Traces (sampling 100% for canary traffic, 1% for baseline) enabled ✅
  - Metric tags for canary=true present on all request metrics ✅
  - Logging redact rules applied for PII ✅
- Stakeholder signoff checklist (sprint lead, SRE, product): get explicit thumbs-up in the #relops channel (screenshot timestamped).

Hour-by-hour sentinel slate (T0 = canary flip) — lean schedule for first 6 hours, then cadence relaxes:
T0: flip canary -> 10% traffic
- 0–15m: confirm ingress routing stable, request counts show expected split (canary ≈ 10% ±1%).
- 0–30m: confirm no spike in 5xx errors; p95 latency sample snapshot (should be within 10% of baseline).
- 30–60m: run targeted quality evals (short prompt set of 20 golden prompts), compare BLEU/ ROUGE-ish heuristics and manual quick-scan for hallucination.

T1 (1h):
- telemetry: p50/p90/p95/p99 summary, error-rate drift, token-per-request distribution.
- heat-check: KV cache hit ratio (should climb vs baseline within first 30m).
- escalate if p95 > 150ms for two consecutive 5m windows or 5xx rate increases > 0.75% above baseline.

T2 (2h):
- increase observational sampling: traces for random 5% of canary requests to capture end-to-end hop timings.
- perf probe: run a synthetic burst (50 rps for 60s) against canary only — watch queueing, OOMs, gpu_utilization.

T3–T6 (3–6h):
- rotate primary observer (ops lead) every 2 hours.
- update run log with any anomalies and actions taken.
- check memory and GPU thermal trends; if rising steadily for >30m, throttle canary traffic to 5% and open DR ticket.

T6–T24 (6–24h):
- cadence: checks every 3 hours, automated snapshot reports every 60m to #relops.
- quality set: run expanded eval (100 prompts) at T12 and T24.

Quick decisioning ladder (symptom -> immediate action):
- Symptom: p95 latency spikes >150ms sustained 10m -> Action: reduce canary to 0% (automatic rollback script: rollback-canary.sh), notify oncall-sre and product, revert model variant if recent model change suspected.
- Symptom: error rate >1% absolute OR >200% relative increase -> Action: reduce traffic to 1%, capture full traces, dump top-10 failing request examples to /tmp/canary-fails, open hotfix PR if fixable config.
- Symptom: quality regression (manual eval shows major hallucination increase) -> Action: pause rollout, route traffic back to baseline model variant, start rollback quality investigation.
- Symptom: GPU OOMs or node panics -> Action: immediate throttle to 0% (safety), escalate to infra oncall, collect node dumps.

Rollback matrix (compact):
- Immediate revert (0–30m): severe infra symptoms above, use automated rollback script.
- Gradual unwind (30m–3h): if borderline perf or oscillating errors, step canary from 10% -> 5% -> 1% while observing.
- Postmortem-driven revert (>3h): if subtle correctness regressions found after longer sampling, perform a config revert and schedule hotfix window.

Telemetry thresholds and alerted signals (for SRE):
- p95 latency > 140ms -> P1 alert channel if sustained 5m.
- request error-rate delta > 0.5% absolute -> warn; >1% -> P1.
- KV cache hit ratio drop > 10% relative -> investigate model/sequence length shift.
- outgoing egress spikes (unexpected region) -> check routing rules.

Run-log template (copy into shift notes) — keep short entries:
- 2026-04-12 09:03 UTC — flipped canary to 10%, observed split 9.8% (ok). — Priya
- 2026-04-12 09:18 UTC — p95 rose to 132ms for 2 intervals (15m). No 5xx. Continuing watch. — Ethan
- 2026-04-12 09:45 UTC — synthetic burst executed; saw queueing at gateway for 90s. Throttled back to 5% for 10m, then scaled canary pool nodes. — Maya

Notes-to-self / open questions (working):
- Validate whether autoscaler cooldown (currently 120s) is too long for rapid microbursts — try reducing to 60s in a future canary.
- Can we push quick probe scripts into the console so oncall can trigger without SSH? (low friction ops).
- Need a small checklist card for customer-success to surface user reports during canary (template included below).

Customer-facing snip (for CS to use):
- "We’re rolling a minor model update to a small % of traffic to validate performance and correctness. If you see any unusual responses, please include the timestamp and a short prompt for debugging. Our team will triage within 1 business hour during the watch window."

Appendix: useful commands and links (copyable) — (put in the run binder)
- rollback: ./scripts/rollback-canary.sh CAN-2026-04-12-a
- synthetic probe: ./scripts/synth-probe.sh --rps 50 --duration 60 --target canary
- trace viewer: https://observability.redwood.internal/traces?tag=canary=true
- dashboard snapshot (auto): https://dashboards.redwood.internal/snapshots/relops/2026-04-12

End of diary snapshot. Keep this doc live during the watch window; annotate with exact timestamps and short notes. After T24 collect the runlog and make a 1-page postmortem if any non-trivial actions were taken.

-- Priya (ops)
